reply:
**Verdict:** `not ready`

The spec is short and readable, but it can't be built as written. Two developers would build undo differently, and the code that already exists (`src/accounts/merge.js`) doesn't record what it moves, so undo isn't possible yet. Most of the gaps are things the spec never decides.

**Findings**

| Severity | Location | Evidence | Suggested direction |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| major | R-4, AC-4; `src/accounts/merge.js:10-11` | The spec says "both accounts are restored", but the code adds the newer account's orders to the older one and empties the newer list (`newer.orders = []`). It doesn't record which orders came from where. Nothing says what happens to orders or notes added to the older account after the merge. | Require a record of what moved. Define what "restored" means when the older account changed after the merge. |
| major | R-4, AC-4 | "Within 30 days". A merge made "30 days ago" can be undone and one made "31 days ago" can't, but 30 days and 5 hours isn't covered. Calendar days or 720 hours, and in which time zone? | State the limit exactly, for example "within 720 hours of the merge timestamp, inclusive". |
| major | R-4 | Nothing says who can undo a merge, and no criterion tests it. | Add a permission rule for undo, probably support-lead only like R-1, and a criterion for refusal. |
| major | Scope, R-2; `src/accounts/merge.js:2` | The spec never says how "older" is decided. The code trusts the order the caller passes the IDs in (`merge(store, olderId, newerId, actor)`) and never checks it. | Say what makes an account older, for example creation date. Say whether the system works it out or rejects reversed input. |
| major | R-3, AC-3 | "An account with an open dispute": the older one, the newer one, or either? AC-3 says only "refused", while AC-1 gives 403. The test data has `disputes: []` (`test/merge.test.js:8`) but nothing defines when a dispute counts as open. | Make it "either account". Give the error code. Define "open". |
| major | R-2, AC-2; `src/accounts/merge.js:10` | R-2 moves "orders, addresses, and notes", but AC-2 checks only orders, and the code only moves orders. | Add criteria for addresses and notes. |
| minor | Failure cases | Some cases aren't covered: merging an account with itself, an ID that doesn't exist (the code would throw a TypeError at `merge.js:10`), an account that's already closed or merged (chains of merges), and two merges running at the same time. | Add a refusal rule and a criterion for each. |
| minor | R-2 | "Closes the newer account with a pointer": the spec doesn't say what the customer sees if they log in with the closed account. That's the problem the spec exists to solve. | Say what happens when someone logs in to a closed account. |
| minor | AC-4 | The second clause ("given one made 31 days ago, then the undo is refused") has no When. | Split it into its own criterion with Given, When and Then. |
| minor | AC-1; `src/accounts/merge.js:4-6` | AC-1 expects an HTTP 403, but the repository has only a function that throws with `error.status = 403`. No route exists. | Say whether this is an API endpoint and where it lives. |
| minor | Non-goals | The only non-goal is "Bulk merges". The spec doesn't say whether customers can merge their own accounts or whether the merge is logged. | Add non-goals, or add an audit requirement (who merged, when). |
| nit | R-1, AC-1, AC-2 | "Users with the support-lead role", "support agent" and "support lead" are used for overlapping groups of people. | Define the role term once and use it throughout. |
| question | Whole spec | `merge.js` already does part of R-1 and R-2. Is the spec meant to extend that code or replace it? | Say which in the spec. |

**Strengths**

- Every requirement has an ID and at least one acceptance criterion linked to it.
- AC-3's "nothing moves" can pass or fail.
- AC-4 tests both sides of the time limit.
- The role name `support-lead` matches the code.

**Questions for the author**

1. If an order was placed on the older account after the merge, where does it go on undo?
2. Can a customer log in with the closed account and get redirected, or is that login turned off?
3. Must every merge and undo be written to an audit log?
4. Is a merge always started by an agent through an API, or are there other ways in?

I can't run commands in this session, so I didn't run the skill's report checker (`scripts/check-review-report.mjs`). I also didn't edit the spec. I can save this report under `docs/` if you want a copy next to the spec.
